requirements.title: End-to-end transport lifecycle
requirements.detail: Support quotation, booking, validation, planning, dispatch, execution, proof of delivery, billing and reconciliation. Track operational, delivery and financial states independently, with controlled transitions for cancellation, partial completion, failure and correction.
acceptance: A valid booking can progress through a dispatched route, recorded delivery evidence and an invoice without re-entering core data.
Failed or partial deliveries remain actionable and preserve their history when rescheduled or credited.

requirements.title: Freight now, mixed operations later
requirements.detail: Model transport work as tasks, stops, resources, schedules and capacity. Freight owns cargo-specific fields; future passenger services can add seats, boarding and accessibility requirements through separate domain models.
acceptance: Freight workflows support collections, deliveries, transfers, returns and multi-leg consignments.
A documented extension design adds a different service type without overloading cargo fields or changing existing freight records.

requirements.title: Multi-depot and subcontracted operations
requirements.detail: Support tenant-owned depots, business units, owned fleets and subcontractors. Keep tenant, customer and subcontractor ownership distinct and enforce access at each boundary.
acceptance: A tenant can plan work across several depots and allocate selected jobs to a subcontractor.
A subcontractor sees only allocated work and permitted evidence, costs and status actions.

requirements.title: Configuration and explicit decisions
requirements.detail: Agree operating countries, cargo types, expected users/jobs/devices, hosting model, availability targets and integration providers before implementation claims. Configure units, currencies, timezones, service types and operating rules without assuming one jurisdiction.
acceptance: The implementation plan records unresolved business decisions with an owner and their effect on delivery.
Country-specific compliance and road-routing suitability have reviewed evidence before being advertised as supported.

requirements.title: Customer and supplier records
requirements.detail: Manage organisations, contacts, collection/delivery sites, billing details, credit terms, contracts and supplier agreements. Version material commercial changes and retain references used by historical jobs.
acceptance: Staff can create and amend authorised customer/site records and find them through search and filters.
Changing a current tariff or address does not silently rewrite an already agreed charge or dispatched stop.

requirements.title: Quotations and rate agreements
requirements.detail: Create quotes with freight quantities, service level, estimated charges, expiry and approval status. Convert an accepted quote into a booking while retaining the agreed terms and commercial audit.
acceptance: An accepted quote produces one linked booking with the quoted cargo and price terms.
Expired or amended quotes require the configured review before conversion.

requirements.title: Consignments and multi-stop orders
requirements.detail: Record customer references, pallets/parcels, weight, volume, dimensions, quantities, handling requirements, service durations and time windows. Separate orders, consignments and transport tasks so split loads and multi-leg journeys are possible.
acceptance: One order can contain several consignments and collection/delivery tasks.
Collections, partial deliveries, returns and transfers retain quantity and custody history.

requirements.title: Booking intake and validation
requirements.detail: Support manual entry, recurring bookings, bulk imports, customer portal and authenticated API intake. Validate addresses, quantities, compatibility, service availability and required information; show field-level errors and import reconciliation.
acceptance: Invalid rows are reported with actionable errors while valid import rows retain traceable source identifiers.
Repeating an idempotent booking request or import retry does not create duplicate work.

requirements.title: Amendments and operational impact
requirements.detail: Apply controlled booking changes with version checks. Changes affecting dispatched work require an operational decision and a new plan/assignment version rather than silently modifying a driver's active manifest.
acceptance: A stale edit is rejected or reconciled explicitly instead of overwriting a newer booking.
Dispatchers can see the impact of changed cargo or delivery windows before approving an updated run.

requirements.title: Road routes and provider capabilities
requirements.detail: Geocode validated locations and obtain road distance/duration matrices and route geometry. Distinguish road routing from fleet optimisation. Verify traffic, truck restrictions, coverage, licensing and routing capabilities for each configured provider.
acceptance: Displayed routes follow supplied road geometry rather than straight lines between stops.
Unresolved addresses or unavailable matrices produce visible actionable failures; unsupported truck capabilities are clearly identified.

requirements.title: Hard and soft constraints
requirements.detail: Check pickup-before-delivery, cargo capacity at every stop, vehicle/equipment compatibility, driver eligibility, shifts, service times, breaks, depots and locked work. Distinguish hard rules from explicitly configured soft preferences and explain infeasibility.
acceptance: No published plan silently violates capacity, pickup precedence or driver/vehicle eligibility.
Every unassigned job has a reason; any soft-rule breach is visible before dispatch approval.

requirements.title: Multi-vehicle optimisation
requirements.detail: Optimise stop order and job allocation across vehicles and depots using configurable cost, distance, duration, priority and empty-mileage objectives. Use bounded background jobs, cancellation and reproducible inputs; validate returned solutions independently.
acceptance: Optimisation returns routes, timing, capacity profiles, cost estimates and unassigned work for the same input version.
Solver failure or timeout leaves existing approved plans intact and makes manual planning available.

requirements.title: Dispatcher workspace and manual planning
requirements.detail: Provide synchronised map, stop list, unassigned jobs and resource availability. Support drag/drop and keyboard alternatives, bulk selection, manual allocation, stop reordering, assignment locks, manifests and clear conflict explanations.
acceptance: A dispatcher can allocate and reorder a run, inspect its feasibility and publish it from one coherent workflow.
Map/list selection stays synchronised and manual edits are validated before publication.

requirements.title: Versioned approval and exclusive reservations
requirements.detail: Preserve proposal, approved and dispatched versions. Recheck current eligibility and reserve jobs/drivers/vehicles at publication using transactional concurrency controls; use explicit approval for replacing dispatched plans.
acceptance: Concurrent attempts to reserve conflicting jobs or resource intervals allow only one valid commitment.
A plan based on stale vehicle availability or driver eligibility cannot be dispatched without revalidation.

requirements.title: Replanning and operational exceptions
requirements.detail: Replan remaining work after delays, breakdowns, failed deliveries or urgent bookings while preserving completed stops, evidence and locked commitments. Present the change set and notify affected users after approval.
acceptance: Replanning cannot erase completed stops or delivery evidence.
Affected drivers receive the approved version and acknowledge material changes; dispatch sees any failed notification.

requirements.title: Android and iPhone driver workflows
requirements.detail: Provide supported Android and iPhone apps for manifests, stop details, navigation handoff, scanning, arrival/departure, quantities, delivery evidence and exceptions. Plan permissions and background behaviour for each platform; native apps run on devices rather than server containers.
acceptance: A driver completes an assigned collection and delivery with POD on both supported mobile platforms.
App release testing verifies permission changes, app restart, low connectivity and background/foreground transitions on real devices.

requirements.title: Offline execution and synchronisation
requirements.detail: Cache authorised assigned work and queue status, GPS and POD updates locally with secure storage, event identifiers and retry controls. Show unsynchronised records, resolve conflicts and clean up revoked or obsolete data under the agreed policy.
acceptance: Offline delivery updates and evidence synchronise once without duplicating business effects.
Drivers can see pending/failed uploads, and stale manifests cannot silently overwrite a new dispatched version.

requirements.title: Authenticated device GPS ingestion
requirements.detail: Register devices and bind credentials to tenant, driver and tracking source. Capture coordinates, accuracy, captured/received times and sequence/event identifiers. Validate payloads, rate limits and authorised tracking sessions; communicate off-duty tracking rules transparently.
acceptance: Another driver or tenant cannot submit or retrieve positions for an unauthorised device/source.
Out-of-order or duplicate positions preserve capture history and do not replace a newer current position.

requirements.title: Live location, freshness and reliability
requirements.detail: Display live/latest location with age, accuracy and source status. Configure sampling and upload policies against battery use, network cost and platform constraints. Handle denied/revoked permissions, disabled services and stale devices without claiming uninterrupted tracking.
acceptance: Dispatch can distinguish fresh, inaccurate, offline, disabled and stale tracking states.
Ending or revoking a tracking session blocks subsequent unauthorised uploads and follows the device retention policy.

requirements.title: Proof of delivery and exceptions
requirements.detail: Capture recipient, signature where required, photographs, timestamps, delivered quantities, damage, shortages and refusal reasons. Keep originals and audit corrections; permit partial completion, return tasks and rescheduling. GPS alone is not POD.
acceptance: Partial/damaged delivery produces the correct remaining work and linked evidence.
Evidence links are authorised and expire as configured; corrections preserve original records and editor identity.

requirements.title: Telematics-ready tracking model
requirements.detail: Use a provider-neutral TrackingSource with effective-dated assignments to drivers/vehicles. Future vehicle devices use the same normalised ingestion contract and source provenance; do not assume a driver's phone position proves vehicle position.
acceptance: Device reassignment attributes positions to the correct subject during the correct interval.
A simulated vehicle-source adapter passes ingestion tests without changing booking or dispatch domain rules.

requirements.title: Driver eligibility and shifts
requirements.detail: Manage driver availability, licences, qualifications, expiry dates, shifts, leave and relevant working/break rules. Support reminders and reviewed jurisdiction-specific calculations.
acceptance: An unavailable or ineligible driver is rejected when committing an assignment.
Expiring qualifications are visible and the configured alerts identify affected future work.

requirements.title: Vehicles, trailers and equipment
requirements.detail: Record dimensions, weight/volume/pallet capacities, equipment, depots, fuel/energy characteristics, operating costs and availability. Model trailer and vehicle combinations where operationally required.
acceptance: Planning evaluates the capacity and compatibility of the assigned configuration.
Unavailable vehicles and incompatible equipment cannot be committed to affected work.

requirements.title: Maintenance, inspections and defects
requirements.detail: Track scheduled maintenance, inspections, defect reporting, repairs, documents and out-of-service periods. Driver-reported defects can create reviewed availability restrictions and fleet follow-up.
acceptance: A defect can be recorded with evidence and traced through its resolution.
An out-of-service decision immediately affects future assignment eligibility and identifies existing affected runs.

requirements.title: Subcontractor allocation and reconciliation
requirements.detail: Manage suppliers, insurance/eligibility records, accepted work, manifests, milestones, POD and agreed costs. Enforce record-limited portal/API access with a clear acceptance and exception workflow.
acceptance: A subcontractor can accept authorised work and return milestones/POD.
Supplier cost reconciliation links to completed work and flags missing evidence or disputed charges.

requirements.title: Rates and accessorial charges
requirements.detail: Support effective-dated rate cards, contract pricing, distance/zone/cargo/service charges and approved extras such as waiting time. Record price inputs, currency, tax configuration and calculation provenance.
acceptance: The same agreed inputs reproduce the stored charge calculation.
Historical prices remain traceable when a current rate card changes, and unauthorised extras cannot be invoiced.

requirements.title: Invoices, credits and accounting
requirements.detail: Review billable jobs, approve charges, generate invoices and credit notes and reconcile accounting exports. Configure numbering and financial rules according to the agreed operating jurisdiction.
acceptance: Repeated billing/export requests do not duplicate invoices or accounting postings.
Credit notes preserve links to the original charge/invoice and their approval reason.

requirements.title: Profitability and operational analytics
requirements.detail: Report on on-time delivery, utilisation, empty mileage, distance, cost, revenue, job/customer profitability and subcontractor performance. Define metric formulas and distinguish planned values from measured or estimated actuals.
acceptance: Report totals reconcile to their underlying authorised jobs and financial records.
Users can filter and drill into metric sources, while tenant isolation also applies to exports.

requirements.title: Documents, retention and compliance evidence
requirements.detail: Manage consignment documents, POD, vehicle/driver records, licences and insurance with versions, expiry alerts, retention and controlled deletion/legal holds where required. Review applicable legal obligations before claiming compliance.
acceptance: Document access, downloads, changes and authorised deletion respect record permissions and retention rules.
Expiry alerts and missing-document exceptions identify the affected operational records.

requirements.title: Customer portal and notifications
requirements.detail: Customers can submit bookings, follow their jobs, retrieve permitted documents and invoices and receive configured notifications. Use durable notification jobs, preferences and visible failure/retry status.
acceptance: A customer can access only their own tenant-authorised bookings, tracking, documents and invoices.
Notification retries do not duplicate domain actions and failures are visible to appropriate staff.

requirements.title: Bounded contexts and shared language
requirements.detail: Establish Bookings, Planning, Dispatch, Execution, Tracking, Resources, Commercial, Integrations and Tenant/Access contexts through workshops. Start with a modular application, independently scalable workers and documented context contracts; deploy separate services only when justified.
acceptance: The code and design document declare each context's owned data, commands, events and dependencies.
Architecture checks prevent direct cross-context persistence access and uncontrolled dependency cycles.

requirements.title: Aggregates, value types and invariants
requirements.detail: Separate orders, consignments, routes, reservations and invoices at their consistency boundaries. Domain methods enforce transitions and business rules. Use tenant-qualified identities and explicit money/currency, quantities/units, coordinates and time-window value types.
acceptance: Domain tests reject invalid transitions and invalid quantities independently of HTTP/UI code.
Exclusive resource reservations remain consistent under real concurrent database transactions.

requirements.title: Ports, adapters and anti-corruption mapping
requirements.detail: Keep maps, GPS providers, ERP/accounting, persistence and messaging behind owned interfaces. External schemas/statuses map into domain commands; provider responses are validated before affecting operational state.
acceptance: A test adapter can replace an external provider without changing domain rules.
Unknown external statuses or invalid provider payloads produce reconciliation errors rather than arbitrary state changes.

requirements.title: Durable events and consistency
requirements.detail: Commit business state with a transactional outbox; use consumer inbox/deduplication and versioned event contracts. Include event identity, tenant scope, type/version, occurrence time and correlation; preserve per-aggregate ordering where the workflow requires it.
acceptance: A crash after commit but before publish eventually delivers the event without losing the business change.
Repeated or out-of-order events cannot duplicate charges or reverse a valid completed state.

requirements.title: Read models and audit history
requirements.detail: Build query models for dispatch and reporting while retaining the authoritative domain state. Keep immutable audit records for sensitive changes and approvals; event sourcing is an explicit optional decision rather than a default requirement.
acceptance: Queries disclose projection freshness where eventual updates affect operational decisions.
Sensitive changes record tenant, actor, before/after reference, time and reason without exposing secrets.

requirements.title: Identity, memberships and least privilege
requirements.detail: Use a reviewed identity approach with MFA for privileged accounts, tenant membership, scoped roles and record/depot/business-unit permissions. Authenticate driver devices and ERP clients independently with rotation and revocation.
acceptance: Users can switch only among authorised tenant memberships and revoked access stops new authorised actions.
Every protected API checks tenant, role and record scope independently of menu visibility.

requirements.title: Isolation across all data surfaces
requirements.detail: Derive tenant scope from validated credentials/membership, not an untrusted request field. Apply isolation to database queries/constraints, files, search, caches, queues, reports, live subscriptions, exports and integration credentials. Use database isolation safeguards with tested non-owner runtime roles.
acceptance: Tenant A cannot read, change, infer through search/export, or subscribe to tenant B's records and GPS/POD.
Background tasks and reused database connections cannot carry one tenant's context into another's work.

requirements.title: Application and container hardening
requirements.detail: Protect transport with TLS and configured storage encryption. Validate inputs, uploads and endpoints; apply request limits, safe session/token handling, dependency/image scanning, secret redaction and scoped service credentials.
acceptance: Security tests cover object-level authorisation, injection, malicious uploads, forged tracking identities and configured request limits.
Secrets are absent from shipped images, browser bundles, logs and public error payloads.

requirements.title: Controlled support and platform access
requirements.detail: Separate platform operation from tenant business access. Exceptional tenant support access is explicitly scoped, time-limited and audited; tenant suspension, exports and deletion have defined retention and review rules.
acceptance: System-admin status does not silently grant unrestricted POD, customer financial or GPS access.
Support access expiry/revocation and privileged changes are tested and visible in the audit.

requirements.title: Privacy, retention and security assurance
requirements.detail: Define collection purpose, authorised tracking periods, access, retention, deletion and incident response with the operating organisation. Review legal/compliance duties for each deployment rather than treating driver consent alone as sufficient.
acceptance: Tracking history and delivery evidence obey the configured retention/hold rules and tenant permissions.
A security review and isolation regression suite gate release, with unresolved findings tracked explicitly.

requirements.title: Documented and versioned APIs
requirements.detail: Publish machine-readable API contracts for customers, bookings, consignments, assignments, milestones, POD metadata and financial exchange. Define pagination, filters, validation errors, rate limits, idempotency and version/deprecation rules.
acceptance: An independent client completes the supported booking/status workflow using the published contract.
Breaking schema changes are detected by contract tests and follow a documented version policy.

requirements.title: Tenant-scoped integration identities
requirements.detail: Create tenant-owned API clients with scoped credentials and external-system connections. Mask secret values, support rotation/revocation and separate read, write, finance and tracking scopes.
acceptance: A client cannot escalate its scopes, choose another tenant or retrieve another connection's secret.
Credential rotation and revocation work without rewriting domain records.

requirements.title: Reliable webhook delivery
requirements.detail: Expose tenant-configured event subscriptions with signed delivery, timestamp/replay validation, event identifiers, payload versions, delivery records, exponential retries, dead-letter handling and authorised replay. Use at-least-once delivery with idempotent consumption.
acceptance: A receiver outage produces visible retry/reconciliation state and eventual delivery after recovery.
Duplicate delivery or authorised replay cannot duplicate the receiver's supported idempotent business outcome.

requirements.title: ERP mapping and reconciliation
requirements.detail: Map external IDs, reference data, status codes and commercial fields per connection. Define ownership and conflict policy, bulk synchronisation checkpoints, reconciliation queues and safe recovery from partial sync.
acceptance: A partially failed synchronisation can resume without creating duplicate jobs or postings.
Conflicting or unknown external values remain visible for review and do not silently overwrite approved operational data.

requirements.title: Endpoint safety and observability
requirements.detail: Validate webhook destinations and inbound/outbound payloads, restrict access to private/internal endpoints as configured, protect signing keys and redact sensitive logs. Display connection health, latency, retry counts and correlation identifiers.
acceptance: Unsafe destinations and unauthorised callbacks are rejected before delivery or processing.
Operators can trace one external request/event through mapping, domain processing and delivery without exposing credentials.

requirements.title: Tenant administration
requirements.detail: Manage tenant members, roles, depots, business units, service settings, branding, operational defaults, integration clients/webhooks, device enrolment, tracking policies and permitted usage settings.
acceptance: A tenant administrator can configure their own operation without infrastructure privileges.
All configuration changes are validated, versioned where relevant and tenant-audited.

requirements.title: System administration
requirements.detail: Manage tenant provisioning/suspension, plan entitlements, quotas, platform defaults, features, deployment health and platform audit. Display usage without exposing unnecessary tenant business content.
acceptance: Provisioning creates an isolated usable tenant and its initial authorised admin workflow.
Quota/feature changes and suspension have defined behaviour for API, drivers and pending background work.

requirements.title: Registered menu catalogue
requirements.detail: Provide system menu defaults and tenant overrides for permitted groups, ordering, labels, icons and role visibility. Menus reference registered application modules/routes; safe external links are explicitly validated.
acceptance: Admins can preview, publish, revert and reset menus for a selected tenant/role.
Arbitrary scripts, unsafe URLs and unknown privileged routes cannot be published through menu configuration.

requirements.title: Permissions and navigation safety
requirements.detail: Resolve menu visibility from module availability, permissions and configured presentation. Preserve essential administration/recovery entries and validate configurations that strand authorised administrators.
acceptance: Hiding or showing a menu never changes API/record permissions or bypasses direct-route authorisation.
A menu update cannot remove the only reachable administration path for its authorised administrator.

requirements.title: Audit and privileged bootstrap
requirements.detail: Avoid production default credentials. Use a one-use bootstrap flow, privileged MFA, scoped support access and clearly recorded administrative actions. Provide searchable audit and reviewed exports.
acceptance: The bootstrap token becomes unusable after initial admin creation and no reusable default password ships.
Privilege changes, deployment actions, menu publication and tenant support access appear in authorised audit views.

requirements.title: Complete reproducible container stack
requirements.detail: Containerise web apps, APIs, tracking ingestion, optimiser/workers, database/spatial capability, cache, durable messaging where used, object storage, ingress, self-hosted identity, monitoring/logging and backup jobs. External map/ERP services remain explicit integrations. Deliver Docker Compose for development and a documented production orchestration profile.
acceptance: A clean supported environment starts the complete declared stack and passes health checks without a host-native database.
Images and configuration are versioned/pinned; data survives ordinary container recreation.

requirements.title: Honest first-install bootstrap
requirements.detail: Provide a signed bootstrap installer or prepared server image that starts the deployment UI and checks the supported runtime. A clean host requires this prerequisite; subsequent configuration, installation and maintenance use the browser wizard.
acceptance: The documented clean-host path reaches the installer UI without requiring hand-written deployment YAML.
Missing runtime, unsupported host, port collisions and insufficient capacity are identified before installation proceeds.

requirements.title: Independent deployment control plane
requirements.detail: Keep the installer/operator console and narrowly authorised deployment agent separate from TMS application availability. Execute predefined release operations rather than arbitrary commands, images or mounts; protect runtime/cluster credentials with separate identity and audit.
acceptance: The console can diagnose or recover a stopped TMS without depending on its API or main database.
Tenant admins and transport services cannot invoke arbitrary deployment-agent or host operations.

requirements.title: Guided deployment and upgrades
requirements.detail: Wizard stages cover release, domain/TLS, storage, backup, initial admin, size, validation, review, deploy and readiness. Preserve configuration on failure. Upgrades verify backup/compatibility, lock deployment, migrate once, roll out and run smoke tests with resumable progress.
acceptance: Repeated or interrupted deployment requests resume safely and do not repeat completed migrations.
A failed readiness check displays its cause and leaves a recoverable previous or explicitly stopped state.

requirements.title: Persistence, backups and recovery
requirements.detail: Use durable encrypted volumes, tested database backups/WAL recovery, document/object backup/version retention and independent backup credentials/storage. Agree recovery objectives, perform restore drills and support validated tenant extraction from an isolated whole-database restore where shared storage is used.
acceptance: A restore drill reconstructs bookings, tracking, financial records and linked documents within the agreed objectives.
Backup freshness, failure, storage exhaustion and recovery verification are visible in the operator console.

requirements.title: Safe migrations and controlled rollback
requirements.detail: Use dedicated locked migration jobs and backward-compatible expand/contract changes. Test fresh and previous-release datasets. Distinguish compatible application rollback from database recovery; destructive changes and schema-incompatible rollback need explicit reviewed workflows.
acceptance: Only one migration job changes the schema during concurrent deployment attempts.
Rollback is blocked or follows the documented recovery path when the previous image cannot use the migrated schema.

requirements.title: Health, scaling and operational security
requirements.detail: Configure startup/readiness/liveness probes, graceful shutdown, bounded workers, resource limits, restricted container privileges, private data-service endpoints and scoped secrets. Define stateful replication/failover explicitly rather than assuming orchestration supplies it.
acceptance: Dependency outages trigger visible degraded status and safe retry/reconnection without corrupting work.
Operational dashboards expose queue age, webhook failure, GPS lag, optimisation time, disk, backup and relevant tenant usage metrics.

requirements.title: Test-driven development
requirements.detail: For each behaviour, define examples, write a failing test, implement and refactor. Keep domain tests fast; use real database integration tests for tenancy/concurrency, API/event contract tests and a small end-to-end suite. Coverage supports review but is not proof of correctness.
acceptance: Each implemented domain behaviour has a reviewed test scenario and passing evidence in CI.
Isolation and reservation tests exercise actual runtime database roles and concurrent transactions rather than mocked persistence.

requirements.title: High-value failure scenarios
requirements.detail: Test cross-tenant access, stale plans, duplicate imports/events, ERP outages, reordered GPS, offline evidence, worker crashes, migrations and backup restore. Use controlled clocks, realistic fixtures and independently checked route feasibility.
acceptance: The suite detects attempted cross-tenant access through APIs, exports, files, caches and live subscriptions.
Crash/retry/offline scenarios complete safely without duplicated bookings, delivery effects or charges.

requirements.title: Operational UI and interaction design
requirements.detail: Use a deliberate design system with readable dense tables, clear hierarchy, synchronised maps/lists, saved filters, bulk actions, drill-down and concise status explanations. Design around dispatcher, driver, customer and administrator tasks; avoid generic decorative dashboards and placeholder controls.
acceptance: Every presented control performs its advertised permitted action with persistent results, validation and feedback.
Representative users complete booking, dispatch, exception handling and admin workflows without dead ends or hidden required information.

requirements.title: Accessibility and responsive behaviour
requirements.detail: Provide keyboard alternatives, visible focus, labelled controls, screen-reader semantics, sufficient contrast and non-colour status cues. Optimise office workflows for desktop and driver workflows for touch; preserve usability across supported viewport sizes.
acceptance: Critical workflows can be completed using keyboard/screen-reader navigation and do not rely solely on drag/drop or colour.
Supported desktop/mobile layouts show actionable validation, status and recovery controls without clipping essential information.

requirements.title: States, errors and real data
requirements.detail: Design explicit loading, empty, offline, stale, permission-denied, conflict and retry states. Preserve recoverable user input, show GPS freshness and report units/timezones consistently; never present invented live or financial data as real.
acceptance: Refresh and interrupted network requests do not silently lose committed changes or conceal pending work.
User-visible demo data, estimates and unavailable integrations are labelled clearly and never reported as implemented production capability.

requirements.title: Milestone evidence and plan maintenance
requirements.detail: Keep a versioned implementation plan linked to requirement IDs, tasks, dependencies and evidence. Start all tasks unstarted. Mark completion only after acceptance evidence; maintain changes from actual development/CI milestones and track decisions, blockers and scope amendments.
acceptance: A completed milestone links to its implemented behaviours and verification evidence.
Automatic plan updates do not mark work complete from elapsed time, optimistic commentary or missing evidence; failed/new checks reopen affected work for review.

milestones.title: Agree the executable specification and architecture
milestones.summary: Confirm operating assumptions, domain boundaries, acceptance examples and the interface direction before implementation.

tasks.title: Confirm scope, scale, jurisdictions and provider decisions
acceptance: Record owners for unresolved countries, cargo, fleet/device scale, hosting, availability and integration decisions.
Approve freight scope and the documented mixed-transport extension model.

tasks.title: Model contexts, aggregates and business state transitions
acceptance: Publish context ownership/contracts and lifecycle diagrams linked to DDD requirements.
Identify reservation concurrency, partial delivery and commercial invariants with executable examples.

tasks.title: Design and review operational and administrative workflows
acceptance: Review dispatcher, driver, customer, installer and admin interaction prototypes.
Define accessible loading/error/offline/conflict states and a consistent navigation catalogue.

tasks.title: Create traceable TDD and milestone foundations
acceptance: Create requirement-to-test/task links and a CI evidence format.
All implementation tasks begin unstarted; progress changes require recorded implementation evidence.

milestones.title: Build the containerised tenant and security foundation
milestones.summary: Establish reproducible infrastructure, identity, tenant isolation and audited administrative boundaries.

tasks.title: Create full Compose stack, CI bootstrap and initial setup UI
acceptance: A clean environment boots app/API, database, storage, workers and declared infrastructure with readiness checks.
CI verifies configuration, migrations on an empty database and persistent data across container recreation.
A minimal first-install UI validates settings and brings up the foundation stack; production upgrade and recovery controls are completed in M09.

tasks.title: Implement identity, tenancy and scoped authorisation test first
acceptance: Tenant membership, MFA-ready privileged identity and scoped service/device credentials are implemented.
Real-database and API tests deny cross-tenant access and detect leaked tenant context.

tasks.title: Implement tenant/system administration and secure bootstrap
acceptance: One-use initial admin setup, tenant provisioning, roles, suspension and audit work end to end.
Tenant admins cannot access deployment operations or platform-only settings.

tasks.title: Implement registered menu management
acceptance: System defaults, tenant overrides, preview/publish/revert and role visibility persist correctly.
Direct-route/API permissions remain enforced and admins cannot strand their administration access.

tasks.title: Establish domain modules, outbox and observability
acceptance: Module boundaries, versioned events and durable commit/publish tests run in CI.
Audit/telemetry redact secrets and carry authorised tenant/correlation context.

milestones.title: Deliver customers, quotations and validated bookings
milestones.summary: Provide usable freight intake through web workflows and traceable imports, with controlled amendments.

tasks.title: Implement customers, suppliers, sites and commercial terms
acceptance: Authorised users create/search/update records with historical references preserved.
Tenant and customer record-scoping tests pass.

tasks.title: Implement quotes and conversion
acceptance: Accepted quotes convert once into linked bookings with agreed cargo/pricing terms.
Expiry, amendment and approval rules have passing domain tests.

tasks.title: Implement orders, consignments and transport tasks
acceptance: Multi-stop, split-load, multi-leg and return examples preserve quantities and references.
Booking states and field validation work through real UI/API flows.

tasks.title: Implement imports, recurring intake and controlled amendments
acceptance: Invalid rows show actionable errors and retrying valid rows cannot duplicate jobs.
Changes to dispatched work require operational review rather than silently rewriting manifests.

milestones.title: Deliver resources and manual dispatch
milestones.summary: Make drivers, vehicles, subcontractors and assignments operational before automated optimisation.

tasks.title: Implement driver, shift and qualification management
acceptance: Availability, expiry and shift restrictions feed assignment eligibility.
Expired/ineligible/unavailable drivers fail commitment tests.

tasks.title: Implement fleet, trailers, inspections and defects
acceptance: Capacity/equipment configurations and out-of-service intervals persist and affect planning.
Defects and maintenance are traceable with evidence and operational follow-up.

tasks.title: Implement coherent manual dispatch workspace
acceptance: Map/list/jobs/resources support keyboard and drag/drop allocation with saved filters.
Manifests, locks and validation feedback work without placeholder actions.

tasks.title: Implement exclusive assignments and versioned publication
acceptance: Conflicting concurrent reservations allow only one valid commitment.
Stale resource/booking versions cannot publish silently; prior dispatched versions remain available.

tasks.title: Implement subcontractor allocation workflow
acceptance: Allocated work can be accepted and tracked under record-limited access.
Supplier eligibility, agreed cost and missing evidence are visible to dispatch.

milestones.title: Deliver road routing and constrained optimisation
milestones.summary: Produce feasible multi-vehicle plans with independently verified routes and controlled replanning.

tasks.title: Integrate validated geocoding and road routing
acceptance: Routes use provider road geometry and distance/duration data.
Coverage/truck capability limitations and provider failures are visible and documented.

tasks.title: Implement constraint model and independent feasibility checker
acceptance: Tests cover pickup precedence, changing load, compatibility, windows, shifts/breaks and locks.
Hard breaches prevent publication and soft breaches/unassigned work show reasons.

tasks.title: Implement bounded asynchronous optimisation
acceptance: Multi-vehicle/depot results include sequence, timing, capacity and estimated costs.
Timeout/cancellation preserves approved plans and offers manual recovery.

tasks.title: Implement reviewable replanning and driver plan versions
acceptance: Completed stops/evidence and locked commitments survive replanning.
Dispatch approves the change set and failed/acknowledged driver updates are visible.

milestones.title: Deliver Android/iPhone execution, GPS and POD
milestones.summary: Complete real-device field workflows with offline recovery and a tracking model ready for vehicle sources.

tasks.title: Build driver manifest and execution workflows on both platforms
acceptance: Supported Android and iPhone devices complete collection/delivery and navigation handoff.
Permissions, restart and foreground/background transitions are tested on real devices.

tasks.title: Implement secure device GPS sessions and live tracking
